extracted.intended_audience: public relations educators, academic program administrators, and practitioners involved in accreditation/certification
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural criteria for evaluating and certifying/accrediting undergraduate and professional public relations programs (ACEJMC accreditation and PRSA CEPR certification), including required competencies, curricular expectations, faculty and resource standards, and site-visit/review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission, Governance and Administration
rubrics_metrics.description: One of ACEJMC's nine standards: evaluates the unit's mission, governance structures, and administrative arrangements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACEJMC accredits academic units (college, school or department) that offer professional programs. Components (e.g., a public relations program) are covered under unit accreditation but not accredited individually. The accreditation process begins with a letter from the institution CEO and proceeds through self-study, site visit, committee review, and council decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curriculum and Instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: ACEJMC standard assessing the quality, structure, and content of the unit's curriculum and instruction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACEJMC 'embraces the value of a liberal arts and sciences curriculum' — compliance requires students to take a minimum of 80 semester credit hours outside the journalism/mass-communications unit, of which 65 must be in liberal arts and sciences. In a typical 120-hour bachelor's degree, public relations students commonly take ~40 semester hours in major-focused courses. Starting fall 2006 the same nine standards apply to professional master's degree programs; ACEJMC evaluates undergraduate and graduate programs separately and may make different recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity and Inclusiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: ACEJMC standard evaluating the unit's attention to diversity and inclusiveness in education and operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACEJMC requires attention to diversity in programs; in forming site-visit teams an effort is made to include a person of color. Diversity also appears among the prescribed student competencies (understanding diversity of groups in global society).

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time and Part-time Faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: ACEJMC standard assessing faculty qualifications, composition, and adequacy of full- and part-time faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes variation across programs where some public relations courses are primarily taught by adjunct and non-tenure-track faculty; accreditation assesses faculty mix and qualifications as part of the standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scholarship: Research, Creative and Professional Activity
rubrics_metrics.description: ACEJMC standard evaluating the unit's scholarship, research activity, creative work, and professional contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses faculty and unit engagement in research, creative activity, and professional scholarship appropriate to journalism and mass communication education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student Services
rubrics_metrics.description: ACEJMC standard evaluating the sufficiency and quality of student services provided by the unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes advising, career services, and other support systems that help students achieve program objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resources, Facilities and Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: ACEJMC standard assessing the adequacy of physical, technological, and financial resources, facilities and equipment for the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Site visit teams examine resources, facilities and equipment as part of evaluating program quality and ability to deliver the curriculum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional and Public Service
rubrics_metrics.description: ACEJMC standard evaluating unit engagement in professional and public service activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses how the unit and faculty serve professional communities and the public, and how service informs instruction and program relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of Learning Outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: ACEJMC standard requiring systematic assessment of student learning outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Self-study should document assessment practices and use of results for improvement; site-visit teams judge compliance/noncompliance with this standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student competency: freedom of speech and press principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must understand and apply the principles and laws of freedom of speech and press, including the right to dissent, to monitor and criticize power, and to assemble and petition for redress of grievances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of ACEJMC's 11 prescribed competencies and values that accredited-unit students must be educated in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student competency: history and role of professionals and institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must demonstrate an understanding of the history and role of professionals and institutions in shaping communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the ACEJMC-prescribed competencies for student education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student competency: diversity in global society
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must demonstrate an understanding of the diversity of groups in a global society in relationship to communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the ACEJMC-prescribed competencies; ties to the Diversity and Inclusiveness standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student competency: concepts and theories of images and information
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must understand concepts and apply theories in the use and presentation of images and information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACEJMC-prescribed competency expecting theoretical understanding and application relevant to communication professions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student competency: professional ethical principles and ethical practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must demonstrate an understanding of professional ethical principles and work ethically in pursuit of truth, accuracy, fairness and diversity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included among the ACEJMC-prescribed competencies; assessment should demonstrate ethical instruction and practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student competency: critical, creative and independent thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must think critically, creatively and independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACEJMC-prescribed competency; assessment of learning outcomes should evidence development of these thinking skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student competency: research and information evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must conduct research and evaluate information by methods appropriate to the communication professions in which they work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACEJMC-prescribed competency; links to Scholarship and Assessment standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student competency: writing correctly and clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must write correctly and clearly in forms and styles appropriate for the communication professions, audiences and purposes they serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACEJMC-prescribed competency; assessment should show students achieve professional writing competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student competency: critical evaluation of work
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must critically evaluate their own work and that of others for accuracy and fairness, clarity, appropriate style and grammatical correctness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACEJMC-prescribed competency emphasizing self- and peer-evaluation skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student competency: basic numerical and statistical concepts
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must apply basic numerical and statistical concepts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACEJMC-prescribed competency to ensure quantitative literacy relevant to communication professions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student competency: tools and technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Students must apply tools and technologies appropriate for the communication professions in which they work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACEJMC-prescribed competency; includes appropriate digital, production, and research technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate-level competency: contribution to knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduate students should be able to contribute to knowledge appropriate to the communication professions in which they will work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACEJMC notes a distinction for graduate/professional master's programs: graduate students are expected to contribute to knowledge, reflecting different expectations from undergraduate competencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-study (production and organization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preparing an extensive self-study organized by the applicable standards (nine standards for ACEJMC) is required as the first major stage of review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The self-study organizes evidence for each standard and is read by the site-visit team prior to the visit; it is a key document used by the Accrediting Committee and Council in making decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site visit: scope and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: A three-day site visit conducted by a team that reads the self-study, examines records, attends classes, and interviews students, faculty and administrators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The team produces a written draft report finding compliance or noncompliance with each standard; visits typically include meetings with stakeholders and direct observation of teaching and facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site-visit team composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Site-visit teams consist of two or more educators and one practitioner, selected from a pool of volunteers who have served previously or undergone training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACEJMC is committed to recruiting team members representative of the unit's disciplines, makes an effort to include a person of color on each team, and includes at least one member who is not a Committee or Council member. PRSA teams are two accredited PRSA members: one practitioner and one educator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Site-visit report and recommendation outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The site-visit team issues a draft and final report and recommends one of three outcomes: accreditation/reaccreditation, provisional reaccreditation, or denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional reaccreditation indicates specified deficiencies that must be corrected within two years, when a revisit will be conducted. The team delivers a draft report to unit administrators and the university CEO before leaving campus; after input, a final report is submitted to headquarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accrediting Committee and Council review process
rubrics_metrics.description: After the site visit, the Accrediting Committee reviews the self-study and team report and forwards recommendations to the Accrediting Council, which makes final accreditation decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee votes and Council decisions occur at annual meetings (committee in March; council in May). There is an appeals process. All ACEJMC meetings are open to the public and votes on accrediting decisions are taken in open sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability of materials and openness
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-studies and site-visiting team reports are available to the public upon request; ACEJMC meetings and votes are open sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency is an expressed principle of ACEJMC's accreditation process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reaccreditation and certification cycle (six years)
rubrics_metrics.description: Units must apply for reaccreditation every six years; PRSA certification is granted for a six-year period and must be repeated for re-certification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both ACEJMC and PRSA use a six-year cycle for reaccreditation/recertification, underscoring periodic re-evaluation and continuous improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unit-level accreditation scope
rubrics_metrics.description: ACEJMC accredits academic units (college, school or department) as a whole; components such as a public relations program are covered under unit accreditation rather than accredited individually.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects programs housed in units not eligible for ACEJMC accreditation (PRSA CEPR targeted such programs originally).

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA certification scope (CEPR): undergraduate public relations programs
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA's Certification in Education for Public Relations (CEPR) is a voluntary program dealing solely with public relations education programs and only at the undergraduate level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CEPR was originally targeted at programs housed in units not eligible for ACEJMC accreditation (e.g., speech communication departments), though few such programs have used it.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA standard: Public Relations Curriculum
rubrics_metrics.description: One of PRSA CEPR's nine standards evaluating the content and structure of the public relations curriculum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRSA reviewers examine curriculum as part of on-site evaluation; certification is based on program compliance with this and other PRSA standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA standard: Public Relations Faculty (Full- and Part-time)
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA CEPR standard assessing qualifications and sufficiency of full- and part-time public relations faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRSA review examines faculty qualifications and their ability to deliver the curriculum effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA standard: Resources, Equipment and Facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA CEPR standard evaluating the adequacy of resources, equipment and facilities supporting the public relations program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRSA reviewers inspect facilities and resources during on-site visits and consider whether they support program objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA standard: Public Relations Students
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA CEPR standard assessing student-related aspects such as recruitment, advising, achievement, and experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes evaluation of student learning and outcomes as observed and documented in the self-study and on-site meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA standard: Assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA CEPR standard requiring assessment of student learning and program effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRSA review includes evaluation of assessment practices and how results are used for program improvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA standard: Relationships with Alumni and Professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA CEPR standard evaluating the program's engagement and relationships with alumni and professional community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRSA reviewers call local professionals and alumni to learn their assessment of the program as part of certification reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA standard: Relationships with Total Unit and University
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA CEPR standard assessing the program's relationships with the larger academic unit and university administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRSA teams meet with department and university administrators to evaluate institutional support for public relations education.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA standard: PRSSA Chapter
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA CEPR standard evaluating the existence and quality of a PRSSA (student society) chapter associated with the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presence of an active PRSSA chapter is a factor in PRSA certification assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA standard: Diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA CEPR standard requiring attention to diversity within the program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PRSA certification assesses how programs address diversity among students, curriculum, and faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRSA review process: reviewers, activities, and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: PRSA CEPR review is conducted by two accredited PRSA members (one practitioner, one educator) who examine curriculum, resources, facilities, faculty qualifications and university support; on-site meetings with stakeholders are conducted and calls are made to local professionals and alumni.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The intensive two-and-one-half day review culminates in a written report and a meeting of the team with the academic vice president and/or the university president. Successful programs are granted certification for six years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to increase practitioner participation and representation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission recommends more public relations practitioners should volunteer to serve on site-visiting teams and more industry organizations should apply for ACEJMC Council membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The report notes PR representation on the ACEJMC Council increased since 1999 but more participation is needed; representation affects voice and votes in accreditation governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of trained volunteers for site visits
rubrics_metrics.description: Selection of site-visit team members favors volunteers who have served on previous teams and/or participated in a training session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACEJMC emphasizes training to increase the number of qualified reviewers; the Arthur W. Page Society, PRSA, the Institute for Public Relations and ACEJMC conduct training programs.
